name: YouTube Probe
description: A test harness, not a product. Answers the open questions in the talk-miner pack with evidence instead of reasoning: will the API hand back an auto-generated caption track, does talk footage (a moving speaker beside slides) need a region mask, and can a YouTube tab be captured with its audio? Seven offline tests need no token, no network and no clicks; eight manual ones need a Google access token or one gesture.
why: The v0.2.92 talk-miner pack rests on two unmeasured assumptions — that ASR captions can be downloaded, and that talk footage defeats the shipped frame metrics. This project has twice shipped a confident number that a real recording immediately falsified. This page measures both before anything is built.

core.note: the metrics under test — masked and unmasked, unchanged
requestAccess — the same GIS helper youtube-editor uses

api.note: window.__tool live after tool:ready. A PROBE SUITE, not a pass/fail suite: most tests ask a question nobody has answered, so `info` is a first-class outcome and every result carries its evidence. Statuses are pass | fail | info | blocked | error, and `error` is load-bearing: it means the HARNESS broke and NOTHING was measured, which must never be reported as the hypothesis failing. Each test states what a pass and a fail MEAN for the v0.2.92 pack, so a result changes the plan rather than colouring a row. A1–A7 need no token, no network and no gesture — they are a real regression suite for the caption parser and the region-mask hypothesis and are safe in CI. M1–M7 and M9 need a Google access token; M8 needs a real click. Access tokens are never returned by any action, only their presence.

events.name: yp:suite:complete
events.detail: { total, pass, fail, info, blocked, error, results }

events.name: yp:auth:changed
events.when: a token is set or sign-in completes

listTests.returns: { tests: [{ id, group, title, hypothesis, needs }] }

runTest.note: never throws — a thrown error IS a result, and losing it to an unhandled rejection would be the worst outcome for a diagnostic

runAuto.returns: Promise<{ total, pass, fail, info, blocked, error, results }>
runAuto.note: A1–A7. No token, no network, no gesture — records a synthetic talk in-page, ~1 minute

runAll.note: everything except M8, which needs a gesture

setContext.note: videoId is one of YOURS (M3/M4); otherVideoId is one you do NOT own (M5–M7, M9). URLs or bare ids both work

getResults.returns: { total, pass, fail, info, blocked, error, results }

getReport.note: leads with the M4 verdict — the question the pack hinges on — and ends with what did NOT run

setToken.note: paste from the OAuth Playground. Never returned by any action

signIn.note: GIS flow via core/youtube-upload requestAccess. Asks for youtube.readonly + youtube.force-ssl

getStatus.returns: Promise<{ running, ran, tests, hasToken, videoId, otherVideoId, token: { scopes, expiresInS, hasForceSsl } | null, channel: { id, title, videoCount } | null }>
getStatus.note: when a token is present this names the signed-in CHANNEL — the acknowledgement that a sign-in reached an account with videos. Cached against the token. Still never returns the token itself

reset.note: clears results AND the cached synthetic clips

limitations: This is a diagnostic page, not the tool the pack describes. It builds nothing and keeps nothing.

The caption parsers live here rather than in core/youtube-api on purpose — promoting a parser before knowing whether it has a source is the extract-before-validating mistake the video-review pack already made once.

A3–A6 measure a SYNTHETIC talk. It carries the traps this project has been caught by (room-tone floor above 0.01, real colour change, a speaker that moves every frame), but it is not a real conference recording and cannot stand in for one.
M8 depends on the browser's tab-audio support, which is a Chromium strength and weaker elsewhere. A 'no-audio-track' verdict is usually a window shared instead of a tab.
Access tokens are held in memory and localStorage for the session. Use a short-lived OAuth Playground token rather than anything long-lived.
